title: THE PHANTOM OVER-DEMAND -- does rho_ph/rho_res scale with M500? (the P2 amplitude FAIL's mass-dependence)

references.G108: the P2 amplitude FAIL: 34/292 (r_M, R500) window bins with rho_dust < 0 on the fixed-A subtraction (peak 1.47 A2029, min 0.286 A644); pooled envelope slope -2.377 -- reproduced here (gate V0c) as the object of the mass-dependence question
references.G098: the free-dust inversion: floor A rho_ph = sqrt(G M_b(<r) a0)/(4 pi G r^2), committed per-cluster median f_dust on [0.2, 1] R500 (0.519-0.843, sample median 0.674) -- reproduced digit-for-digit (gate V0b) and used as the f_dust anchor
references.G075: r_M = sqrt(G M_b(R500)/a0); T_ratio 0.28 gate; the G050/G057 ingest convention
references.G095_G104: the temperature ratio packages the deficit; not used for the ratio itself, only cited for context

definitions.r_M: sqrt(G M_b(R500)/a0)/KPC (G075/G108 convention; baryons at R500)
definitions.window: shells of the committed M_FORW grid with midpoint in (r_M, R500) (G108's exact binned_profile)
definitions.footing_A: rho_ph = A_cl/r^2, A_cl = sqrt(G M_b(R500) a0)/(4 pi G) -- the r_M-equipartition reading (G03E: M_ph(<r_M) = M_b(R500))
definitions.footing_B: rho_ph = sqrt(G M_b(<r) a0)/(4 pi G r^2) -- G098's floor A, per-bin baryons (the G098-comparable reading)
definitions.ratio: rho_ph/rho_res, rho_res = rho_tot - rho_b (shell densities); ratio > 1 = the phantom over-demands (negative dust)
definitions.f_dust: 1 - <ratio>_window: the free-dust fraction of the missing mass on the window (G098's definition per radius, window-mean)

data: committed X-COP ingests, real_research/data/xcop/ (identical loader to G098/G108); M500/R500 from xcop_r500_ettori2019.json (Ettori+19); the G098 anchor read from the committed deepseek_push/G098_results.json

V1.statement: THE MASS-DEPENDENCE: the pooled resolved-bin relation log10(ratio) vs log10(M500) on footing A (fixed A/r^2, the equipartition reading) has Pearson rho = +0.099 (p = 0.097), Spearman = +0.079 (p = 0.185), slope +0.127 +- 0.099 dex/dex over 284 resolved bins -- at most a BORDERLINE positive trend (bins are clustered in 12 systems; the honest per-cluster reading below is weaker).  Footing B (per-bin M_b) shows rho = +0.242, p = 0.000 (same caveat).  At FIXED r/R500 the cross-cluster slopes are consistent with zero at every slice (median +0.02 dex/dex over x = 0.35-0.95, all p > 0.3); the window-mean relation gives rho = +0.260 (p = 0.415), Spearman = +0.322 (p = 0.308) on n = 12 clusters, and Spearman(over-demand fraction, M500) = +0.266 (p = 0.403).  THE THRESHOLD QUESTION: over-demand bins (ratio > 1) appear in 4/12 clusters spanning M500 = 4.63-8.82 e14 (A2029 8.8, A2319 7.3, A644 5.7, A1795 4.6) -- DOWN TO A1795 at 4.63 e14 (rank 9/12) while A2142 at 8.95 e14 and ZW1215 at 7.66 e14 (its demand is the LOWEST of the sample) never over-demand; a clean mass threshold would need A1795 below M_* and A2142/ZW1215 above it.  The fitted window-mean crossing ratio = 1 at M_* = 69.4 e14 is UNCONSTRAINED (1-sigma bracket 0.0-195948.1, lower slope branch never crosses).  VERDICT: NO clean M_* -- the over-demand is NOT mass-selected (it is radius-selected: every over-demand bin sits at x >= 0.59 R500); the trend is weakly positive, not monotonic-significant.

V2.statement: f_dust(M500) = 1 - <rho_ph/rho_res>_window: per-cluster values -0.09-0.51 (footing A, geometric window-mean), median 0.362 vs G098's committed [0.2, 1] R500 medians (sample median 0.674): median delta = -0.342 (A) / -0.091 (B), 12/12 clusters at or below G098; Pearson rho(f_dust_A, M500) = -0.284 (p = 0.371), Spearman = -0.322 (p = 0.308); rho(delta_A, M500) = +0.319 (p = 0.313)

V3.statement: THE HONEST STATEMENT -- what the phantom's over-demand says about the equilibrium's validity range at cluster scale: the phantom's demand rho_ph/rho_res does NOT robustly scale with M500 (pooled-A Pearson rho = +0.10, p = 0.10; fixed-r/R500 slopes median +0.02 dex/dex across x = 0.35-0.95, all p > 0.3; window-mean p = 0.41 on 12 clusters).  The over-demand is confined to 26 resolved bins in 4/12 clusters, every one at x = 0.59-0.99 R500 (the OUTER window, where the residual density is thinnest and the inversion is closest to G098's censored tail), and the over-demanding set spans A1795 (4.63 e14, rank 9/12) through A2029 (8.82 e14) while A2142 (8.95 e14, the most massive) and ZW1215 (7.66 e14, the LOWEST demand of the sample) never over-demand: there is NO mass threshold, and the window-mean equilibrium is consistent in 11/12 clusters (the single exception, A2319, is driven by its last resolved shells at x ~ 0.94-0.99).  the fitted M_* = 69.4 e14 is unconstrained (1-sigma bracket 0.0-195948.1; the lower slope branch never crosses ratio = 1), so NO mass limit is measured -- VERDICT ON THE EQUILIBRIUM AT CLUSTER SCALE: the r_M-equipartition is TOO STRONG in an outer-bin tail that is RADIUS-selected (every over-demand bin at x >= 0.59 R500), not mass-selected -- the two-regime architecture's mass limit at cluster scale is NOT established on this sample: the phantom over-demands in an outer-bin tail whose per-cluster severity correlates only weakly with mass (Spearman(over-demand fraction, M500) = +0.27, p = 0.40), and the per-bin floor B (G098's own footing) reproduces the same outer bins (e.g. A2029 x = 0.67-0.93, ratios to 1.28) -- the over-demand is a real but per-cluster, outer-region phenomenon, not a mass-selected regime boundary.  NOT CLAIMED: that the equilibrium is wrong anywhere -- the window-mean demand stays inside the residual for 11/12 clusters, and the borderline pooled trend (A ~ M_b(R500)^(1/2) predicts demand rising with mass) is consistent with the data within its spread; the claim that FAILS is the threshold M_*: it is not measured here.
